Definition: from G1093; a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a friend:--neighbour.
BiblicalUsage: The plain sense of geítōn is neighbour. It comes up 4 times, and the passages from Luke and John show how steadily Scripture uses it. I do not find a second, secret meaning hiding behind it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that geítōn matters because loving my neighbour is not an extra to the faith — it is the faith, lived out. I read this as a reminder that God’s words mean what they say, and I can trust them.
